newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle active at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle active at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets Thursday were active, with sales at $72.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from Wednesday and up $2.00 from last week's top price, feedlot sources said.
About 30,000 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 10,000 in Kansas, they said.

Some of the cattle sold had a few extra delivery days attached beyond the normal seven-day delayed delivery period, the feedlot sources said. Extra days implied packers were anticipating strong beef demand and wanted to ensure they had cattle to fill orders, the sources said.
Feedlot cattle prices were supported by tight supplies of finished cattle and projections for shorter numbers next week.
Strong boxed beef demand this week lent further support, although there was talk that beef prices may be near a top.

Week to date sales from Friday to Thursday in the Panhandle set a record large volume at 192,700 head, breaking the previous weekly record of 155,400 during the week ended Aug 22 this year. Some sources discounted the record saying the market was working off of two week's worth of showlists since the weekly total includes last Friday's brisk sales, which came at the end of a slow week, sources said.
